text:
Site A "Brookfield": Franklin County, PA. 100 MW solar + 50 MW storage, target COD 2030. Former industrial land we control, already zoned industrial. Substation is 1.5 miles away on our own land (1 parcel). No wetlands, no homes nearby, no objections we know of.
Site B "Ridgeview": Sussex County, VA. 100 MW solar + 50 MW storage, COD 2030. Greenfield farmland next to a subdivision. Gen-tie route is 6 miles across 4 parcels. No wetlands mapped. Neighbors objected to another solar farm at a county hearing last year.
Site C "Meadow Creek": Clinton County, OH. 100 MW solar + 50 MW storage, COD 2030. Greenfield near a creek with a mapped wetland crossing. Connection route not confirmed yet. Homes nearby unknown.

site.name: Brookfield
site.notes: Land is controlled by developer and zoned industrial; substation is on the same land.

drivers.label: Lower upgrade signal
drivers.reason: 35th percentile across 14 county studies supports lower exposure.

drivers.label: Restudy cost spread
drivers.reason: Spread is one-and-a-half times median, with no shared substations.

drivers.label: Short direct route
drivers.reason: One-and-a-half miles and one parcel meet lower-risk thresholds.

drivers.label: Industrial site
drivers.reason: Former industrial, industrially zoned land avoids greenfield concerns.

drivers.label: Few community signals
drivers.reason: No nearby homes or objections; county withdrawals trail the state rate.

result.summary: No statewide siting authority for solar. Municipal zoning ordinances decide where projects can go. Construction disturbing 1+ acre needs a DEP NPDES stormwater permit.

site.name: Ridgeview
site.notes: No wetlands mapped; site is next to a subdivision; neighbors objected to another solar farm at a county hearing last year.

drivers.label: Elevated upgrade risk
drivers.reason: Sussex ranked at the 92nd percentile of PJM studies.

drivers.label: Shared upgrade exposure
drivers.reason: Two shared substations and high active capacity increase reallocation risk.

drivers.label: Difficult connection route
drivers.reason: Six miles and four parcels make the route more challenging.

drivers.label: Local approval scrutiny
drivers.reason: Farmland faces local review under a local-veto regime.

drivers.label: Documented local opposition
drivers.reason: Neighbors objected at a county hearing, with homes nearby.

card.next_action: Confirm route and upgrade exposure with utility

result.summary: Local zoning approval (conditional or special use permit) plus a comprehensive-plan review are required. Localities can negotiate siting agreements. State DEQ Permit by Rule covers solar up to 150 MW.

site.name: Meadow Creek
site.notes: Site is near a creek with a mapped wetland crossing; connection route is not confirmed.

drivers.label: Limited county evidence
drivers.reason: One county study limits confidence despite its 39th-percentile result.

drivers.label: Shared upgrade exposure
drivers.reason: One shared substation reaches 300 MW; county withdrawal rate is 100%.

drivers.label: Route unconfirmed
drivers.reason: Distance and parcel crossings are unknown; route is not confirmed.

drivers.label: Wetland and veto risk
drivers.reason: Wetlands are present, and Ohio allows county bans on large solar.

drivers.label: Community outlook unknown
drivers.reason: Nearby homes and local objections are both unknown.

result.summary: Projects of 50 MW or more need an OPSB certificate. Under SB 52 (2021), county commissioners can ban large solar in unincorporated areas and sit on the OPSB panel for the case.

portfolio.headline: Prioritize Brookfield; Meadow Creek ranks ahead of Ridgeview on fewer higher-risk ratings.
